title: Local-Minima-Preserving Polynomial Relaxation of Ising Problems
claim: Parameterized attractor families can be tuned to produce double-well landscapes whose depth and curvature are controlled by a single parameter.
layout: 3 panels, 2 on top and 1 wide below, shared line-plot style
description: Three line-plot panels show the attractor function family A_f(x) against x. The top-left panel, f_θ1(x), shows concave downward parabolas peaking at zero. Four curves are labeled θ=0.5, 1.0, 2.0 and 0.2, and larger θ gives a steeper drop. The top-right panel, f_θ2(x), shows double-well curves. Four parameter settings (α, β, k) give a flat or shallow center, with minima near x=±1 to ±1.4 and steep walls that rise sharply near |x|≈1.8. The wide bottom panel, f_θ3(x), shows smoother, flatter curves with shallow wells near x=±2 for some settings and a downward parabola for another. A purple-to-orange palette distinguishes curves. Legends sit inside each plot. The eye goes first to the top-right panel, where the wells are most pronounced.
caption: Plot of the class of attractor functions: fθ1, fθ2 and fθ3 for various parameter values θ. Both physics-inspired attractors fθ2 and fθ3 exhibit a double-well structure, with θ controlling the depth and curvature of the wells.
abstract: The generalized Ising problem captures a broad spectrum of hard combinatorial problems, including MAX-CUT, Number Partitioning (NPP), and Maximum Independent Set. In this work, we consider the notion of one-flip local minima for this problem. We construct a polynomial relaxation and prove the landscape equivalence theorem: there exists a one-to-one correspondence between the local minima of the relaxation and the one-flip local minima of the original Ising problem. This guarantee reduces the Ising problem to finding the local minima of a smooth function, allowing us to leverage scalable gradient-based optimizers such as ADAM. We demonstrate that our method achieves strong performance across challenging benchmarks, including spin-glass models, MAX-CUT, and NPP.
